hook.convey: one whole shared into EQUAL parts → each part gets a name from how many equal parts the whole has: 4 equal parts → 1/4; a roti shared at home, a paper strip folded for a drawing

use.hi: Ghar mein ek roti 4 bachchon mein barabar baantni hai. Har hisse ka ek naam hota hai.
use.en: At home one roti is to be shared equally among 4 children. Each part has a name.

use.hi: Drawing ke liye kaagaz modo ya ghar mein roti baanto: har barabar hisse ka ek naam hota hai.
use.en: Fold paper for a drawing or share a roti at home: each equal part has a name.

explain.convey: roti in 4 equal parts → one part = 1/4 = one of 4 equal parts = a fractional unit; the bottom number = how many equal parts the whole has; the card: a same-size roti in 8 equal parts on its own board → the child names its unit

viewCaption.hi: Yahan wahi roti ek seedhi patti ki tarah khuli hai: 4 barabar hisse, aur ek hisse mein rang.
viewCaption.en: Here the same roti is opened out like a straight strip: 4 equal parts, and one part coloured.

point.hi: Yeh roti 4 barabar hisson mein bati hai. Rang wala ek hissa poori roti ka 1/4 hai. Poore ke barabar hisson mein se aisa ek hissa fractional unit kehlata hai.
point.en: This roti is in 4 equal parts. The coloured part is 1/4 of the whole roti. One such part out of a whole's equal parts is called a fractional unit.

pointAlt.hi: Socho chaar dost yeh roti barabar baant-te hain. Har dost ke haath chaar barabar hisson mein se ek aata hai, jaise yeh rang wala hissa: roti ka 1/4. Aise ek hisse ko fractional unit kehte hain.
pointAlt.en: Picture four friends sharing this roti equally. Each friend gets one of the four equal parts, like this coloured part: 1/4 of the roti. One part like that is called a fractional unit.

prompt.hi: Ab bagal wali roti dekho, utni hi badi, par 8 barabar hisson mein bati. Uska ek hissa kaunsa fractional unit hai?
prompt.en: Now look at the roti beside it, just as big, but in 8 equal parts. Which fractional unit is one of its parts?

whyShort.hi: roti ke 8 barabar hisse, aur yeh unmein se ek

whyAlt.hi: Aath dost yeh roti barabar baantein, toh har dost ke haath aath barabar hisson mein se ek aata hai: 1/8.

point.en: Now look at two strips, each in 3 parts. A's three parts are equal, so each part is 1/3. B's parts are big and small, so we can't call them 1/3 by counting the parts.

say.hi: 2 roti 5 bachchon mein: har roti ke 5 barabar hisse karo, aur har bachche ko har roti se ek hissa do. Jitni roti hain, har bachche ko utne hi hisse milte hain.
say.en: 2 rotis among 5 children: cut each roti into 5 equal parts, and give each child one part from every roti. Each child gets as many parts as there are rotis.

simpler.hi: Har roti se har bachche ko ek-ek hissa do, aur phir ek bachche ke hisse gino.
simpler.en: Give every child one part from each roti, and then count one child's parts.

sayAlt.hi: Likhne se pehle ek baat jaancho: roti bachchon se kam hon, toh kisi ko poori roti nahi milti, aur hissa 1 se kam hota hai. Ulti likhi bhinn 1 se zyada ho jaati hai, isliye woh galat hai.
sayAlt.en: Before writing, check one thing: if there are fewer rotis than children, nobody gets a whole roti, and the share is less than 1. A fraction written upside down comes out more than 1, so it is wrong.

prompt.hi: Do ek jaisi roti 3 bachchon mein barabar baanti gayi, aur waisi hi 2 roti 5 bachchon mein. Kis group ke har bachche ko zyada roti mili: 3 bachchon wale ya 5 wale?
prompt.en: Two identical rotis were shared equally among 3 children, and 2 more just like them among 5 children. In which group did each child get more roti: the 3 children's or the 5's?

reask.hi: 2 roti 3 bachche baantein, aur waisi 2 roti 5 bachche: kahan ek bachche ka hissa bada hai?
reask.en: 3 children share 2 rotis, and 5 children share 2 rotis just like them: where is one child's share bigger?

did.hi: do groups mein baanti roti ke hisse nikal kar unki tulna ki
did.en: worked out the shares of roti in two groups and compared them

why.hi: Dono groups mein har bachche ko har roti se ek hissa mila, yaani 2 hisse. 3 bachchon mein har hissa 1/3 hai aur 5 mein 1/5, aur 1/3 bada hai, toh 2/3 roti 2/5 se zyada hai.
why.en: In both groups each child got one part from each roti, so 2 parts. Among 3 children each part is 1/3 and among 5 it is 1/5, and 1/3 is bigger, so 2/3 of a roti is more than 2/5.

simpler.hi: Pehle socho, har group mein ek bachche ko kitni roti milti hai. Phir dekho kiske hisse bade hain.
simpler.en: First think how much roti one child gets in each group. Then see whose parts are bigger.
